commands.name: feature
commands.description: Works with the features of the application in the current directory

commands.name: add
commands.description: Adds features to the application in the current directory: its files and its record become those of an application that was created with them. A feature the application already has is left as it is. A feature takes the place of one the application has by default, as postgres takes that of h2, and the command says which it replaces; a feature that was asked for by name, when the application was created or added to, is replaced only with --replace, and an option the application was created with is never replaced. The files you changed keep your changes. When a feature changes or takes out what you changed too, or a file it writes is there already, nothing is written and the files are named. An application with the feature of a feature pack that is not part of Grails gets a feature only with that very pack: the jar of a plugin is fetched again by the coordinates and the SHA-256 its record has, and the pack of a directory is given again with --feature-pack-dir.

commands.name: list
commands.description: Lists the features of the application in the current directory, from its record: those it has, which of them were asked for by name, the features feature add can add to it, and for each of the others why it cannot. Outside a project the features an application can be created with are listed by the create commands, with --list-features.

commands.name: project
commands.description: Works with the record of how the application in the current directory was generated

commands.name: show
commands.description: Says how the application in the current directory was generated: its type, name and package, its options, the features that were asked for and left out, and every feature it has. Every option of the create command is listed with the value the record has for it, also one that was not given, and with whether that value is the default of this version of the command line: a default can change from one version to the next. The last line is the command that creates the application again, with the version of the command line that generated it.

commands.name: regenerate
commands.description: Generates the application in the current directory again as its record says it was generated, and changes nothing in it. With --output the application is written to another directory, whose record is then that of this one. With --diff nothing is written, and the files of this application that are not what was generated are named: those that were added, removed and changed.

commands.name: migrate
commands.description: Writes the record of the application in the current directory, for an application that has none: one that was created with the Grails shell or by an earlier version, or was not generated at all. The commands that create its classes are there once it has the record. What the application is, is worked out from its files, which are read and not changed: the record an earlier version wrote, the profile it had, the plugins and the dependencies of build.gradle, and its configuration. What was found, where, and what was assumed is said; the options say it otherwise. Only the directory .grails is written to. The record says that it was written for an application that was there. No feature is added to such an application by a command, and it is not generated again: there is no copy of what the generator wrote to tell its changes from yours.

commands.name: gradle
commands.description: Runs Gradle in the Grails project of the current directory, with the Gradle wrapper of the project. Everything after gradle is given to Gradle as it is, the options too. So gradle --help is the help of Gradle, and this text is what help gradle shows.

commands.name: help
commands.description: Shows how a command is used, or without a command which commands there are here. For a command of a command give both names, as in help feature add.

commands.name: compile
commands.description: Compiles the sources of the Grails project: the Gradle task classes. What follows -- is given to Gradle as it is.

commands.name: clean
commands.description: Deletes what the build of the Grails project has produced: the Gradle task clean. What follows -- is given to Gradle as it is.

commands.name: assemble
commands.description: Creates the JAR or WAR archive of the Grails project for deployment. Runs the Gradle task assemble, for the production environment unless -Dgrails.env names another one. What follows -- is given to Gradle as it is.

commands.name: dependency-report
commands.description: Prints the dependencies of the Grails project: the Gradle task dependencies. What follows -- is given to Gradle as it is.

commands.name: test-app
commands.description: Runs the tests of the Grails project. Runs every test phase of the project, which are the Test tasks of its build, the ones the project adds among them, for the test environment unless -Dgrails.env names another one: the Gradle task testApp. A phase is selected by a switch of its name: --unit and --integration, and for another phase the name of its task without the ending Test, as --functional for functionalTest. Several can be given. What follows -- is given to Gradle as it is.

commands.name: stats
commands.description: Prints how many source files the Grails project has, and how many lines of code, by the kind of class

commands.name: bug-report
commands.description: Creates a ZIP file of the sources of the Grails project. It is to attach to an issue, holds what is under grails-app and src, and build.gradle, and is written to the build directory. The configuration under grails-app/conf is in it as it is: look through the ZIP for passwords before it is given to anyone.

commands.name: run-app
commands.description: Runs the Grails application: the Gradle task bootRun. Stays with the application until it ends or the command is cancelled. With --detach, and in the interactive shell, returns when the application answers on its port and leaves it running until stop-app. The environment is development unless -Dgrails.env names another one. What follows -- is given to Gradle as it is.

commands.name: stop-app
commands.description: Stops the Grails application that run-app started for this project. A run-app that stays with the application is asked to end its build, and does. Of a run-app that left the application running, the Gradle it started is ended, and with it every process below it. The application ends with the build: the Gradle daemon that runs the build ends what the build started. The command then waits until nothing takes connections on the port of the application any more, and says so when the application had not taken its port yet: its end is then not seen. Nothing else is ended: a process is ended, or asked, only when it is the one run-app recorded in .grails/run.

commands.name: console
commands.description: Runs the Swing console of the Grails application: the Gradle task console. Stays with the console until it is closed. The environment is development unless -Dgrails.env names another one. What follows -- is given to Gradle as it is.

commands.name: shell
commands.description: Runs the Groovy shell of the Grails application: the Gradle task shell. What is typed goes to the shell until it is left. The environment is development unless -Dgrails.env names another one. What follows -- is given to Gradle as it is.

commands.name: run-script
commands.description: Runs Groovy scripts in the Grails application: the Gradle task runScript. The application is started around the scripts, without a web server. The environment is development unless -Dgrails.env names another one. What follows -- is given to Gradle as it is.

commands.name: run-tool
commands.description: Runs a tool of the Grails application: the Gradle task runTool. NAME is a tool of the application or of one of its plugins, which is run with the application started around it, or without the application when the command is one that needs none. Everything after NAME is given to that tool as it is, also what looks like an option of this one. The environment is development unless -Dgrails.env names another one, before NAME.

commands.name: update-wrapper
commands.description: Replaces the Grails wrapper of the project by that of this version of Grails. The wrapper is the files grailsw, grailsw.bat and grails-wrapper.jar, which are committed with the project. Typed to the wrapper (./grailsw update-wrapper), the command line of the version the project names is downloaded again first.

commands.name: list-plugins
commands.description: Lists the Grails plugins: those of this release of Grails, and those of the plugin index of Grails, which is read from the network. Each has its name, its coordinates, the latest version for this Grails and what it is for; plugin-info says more of one.

commands.name: plugin-info
commands.description: Says what is known of one Grails plugin: its versions, what it is for, its license, where its documentation, issues and sources are, and the line that adds it to the build of an application. list-plugins lists the plugins.
